description: One ci-observe E2E capture at a time: pick it with the Run variable (Loki label osac_ci_capture_id, newest first). Read top to bottom: Run overview says what ran and whether it passed, the collapsed Run identity row holds the exact refs when expanded, Collection coverage says how complete the telemetry is, the collapsed CI evidence row holds the GitHub job, step and JUnit evidence, then Tests and workers, Fixture work, Waits and Service requests break the run down, and the collapsed Environment row holds the pod and node metrics. Keep the default 7-day time range while picking a capture, because a narrower range can hide a run whose trace is only partly inside the window.

panels.title: Run overview
panels.description: Read this first: what the run was, whether it passed, and how long it took. A missing session span means the outcome is unknown, not passed.

panels.title: Tests
panels.description: Parent pytest test spans (pytest.span_type = test, ::setup/::call/::teardown phase spans excluded). Tempo returns at most 100 spans per trace, so runs with more than 100 tests are undercounted here. Zero means no test spans were recorded, which is not evidence of a pass - see Run result.

defaults.noValue: No test spans in this capture

panels.title: Failed
panels.description: Test spans with status = error, set by pytest-opentelemetry on failures. A zero here is only meaningful together with a non-zero Tests count and a recorded Result; without those, zero means 'not recorded', not 'passed'. GitHub still owns the final job conclusion.

panels.title: Result
panels.description: Status of the pytest session span: error means at least one test failed during the run. 'Incomplete: no session span' means the outcome was never captured here, so it is unknown, not passed. GitHub's job conclusion stays authoritative; use the job evidence link under Collection coverage.

panels.title: Session
panels.description: Whether the pytest session span arrived: 1 means Complete, 0 or no data means Incomplete - the run's outcome and duration were never captured, so Failed showing zero is not evidence of a pass. Check the GitHub job for the real result.

panels.title: Test time
panels.description: Elapsed time from the start of the test session to its end. 'not recorded' means the session span never arrived.

panels.title: Suite
panels.description: Suite label (osac_ci_suite) carried on the capture's Loki streams; shows 'not labeled' for captures imported before suite labels existed.

panels.title: PR
panels.description: Pull-request label from the capture's Loki streams. The value `none` is shown as `No PR`.

panels.title: Collection coverage
panels.description: How complete this capture's telemetry is. Counts are lower bounds: Tempo returns at most 100 spans per trace and 30,000 traces per search. The panel below links the GitHub job and native pytest evidence, which stays authoritative.

panels.title: Parent test spans
panels.description: Parent pytest test spans in the capture. Zero means no test spans were recorded. Tempo returns at most 100 spans per trace, so runs with more than 100 tests in one trace are undercounted.

panels.title: Wait spans
panels.description: Spans the test suite recorded while waiting for the cluster (poll_until waits). Tempo returns at most 100 spans per trace, so long runs are undercounted.

panels.title: Service spans
panels.description: Named service operations recorded by Beyla (gRPC calls, HTTP routes, Redis and database commands), excluding pytest spans and wait spans. Busy captures exceed Tempo's 30,000-trace search cap, so this is a lower bound.

panels.title: Where is the rest of the evidence?
panels.description: Links to the dashboards that own the evidence this one cannot show, and the deliberate scope gap for cluster evidence.

options.content:
- **GitHub job conclusion, step logs and the native pytest report**: expand the **CI evidence** row below on this page. Traces never override GitHub's job conclusion.
- **What the cluster did during the run**: expand the **Environment** row at the bottom of this page for pod CPU, memory and pod lifetimes, from kubelet metrics sampled once a minute.
- **Compare with another run**: open the [run comparison dashboard](/d/ci-observe-compare-runs/ci-observe-compare-runs?orgId=1) and pick a cohort there; it does not take a single capture id.
- **Cluster events and pod logs** still have no readable view here: Kubernetes events are stored but unread, and the collector cannot read pod logs. The captured pod logs are in Loki: [query them in Explore](/explore?orgId=1&left=%7B%22datasource%22%3A%22ci-observe-logs%22%2C%22queries%22%3A%5B%7B%22expr%22%3A%22%7Bosac_ci_capture_id%3D%5C%22$capture_id%5C%22%7D%22%2C%22refId%22%3A%22A%22%7D%5D%2C%22range%22%3A%7B%22from%22%3A%22now-7d%22%2C%22to%22%3A%22now%22%7D%7D) with `{osac_ci_capture_id="$capture_id"}`.

panels.title: CI evidence
panels.description:
GitHub-side evidence for this capture, read top to bottom: **Run** and **Jobs** say what GitHub recorded, **Steps** breaks down where the time went, **JUnit summary** is the native pytest result, and **Failed tests** lists the failures with a link to the artifact.

**If a panel shows "Not deployed or unavailable", a query error, or no content at all**, the native evidence was not loaded. The workflow-exporter endpoint is either not deployed or unreachable, or the artifact is gone; this is not a passing result. Grafana does not replay an errored query to panels that mount after it failed, so a far-down table can render no content at all rather than an error.

**Where the data comes from.** Job and step data is the workflow exporter's GitHub job history (SQLite, 60-day retention). Native test data is the JUnit XML inside the run's `osac-logs-[<suite>-]full-install-<run id>` artifact, fetched on demand and cached for 15 minutes. GitHub keeps workflow artifacts for 7 days; past that the status is `expired` and the counts stay empty, never a green zero.

**States the native panels can show.** `unavailable` is a dashboard display state, not a status the endpoint returns: the workflow-exporter endpoint is not deployed or unreachable, so no native evidence was loaded at all. `available`: the JUnit file was parsed, so the counts are real. `missing`: no artifact matching the osac-logs full-install pattern exists. `expired`: the artifact passed its 7-day retention. `too_large`: the artifact is above the 64 MiB download bound. `invalid`: the artifact was downloaded but holds no readable `junit.xml`. `not_requested`: nothing was looked up.

**Limits.** Step durations are the wall-clock time between a step's start and end, not runner minutes, and a skipped or cancelled job has no steps at all. No automatic root-cause diagnosis is generated: the failed-test messages are raw JUnit output. They show what failed; they are not a root-cause diagnosis. Re-runs overwrite the artifact, so an older attempt may show the newest attempt's native results.

panels.title: Run
panels.description: The workflow run itself. Commit is fetched from GitHub on demand and can be empty when that fetch fails. Open the GitHub run from the last column.

panels.title: Jobs
panels.description: The stored job rows of this run and attempt: the run's own row, plus each suite row for pull-request flow runs. Open a job on GitHub from the last column.

panels.title: Steps
panels.description: Every stored step of the run's jobs, with the job it belongs to. Conclusion is failure when the step name appears in the job's failed-step text; otherwise it was not recorded per step.

panels.title: JUnit summary
panels.description: One row: the native status, the JUnit counts and total time, the artifact link, and the notes explaining any gap. The root selector is a JSONPath because the Infinity parser replaces a plain object root with its first nested array.

panels.title: Failed tests
panels.description: At most the first 100 failed tests are listed; messages are capped at 2000 characters and stack traces are never included. Empty when the run passed, or when the artifact is missing, expired or too large.

defaults.noValue: No failed tests, or no JUnit evidence: check the JUnit summary Status row.

panels.title: Run identity (source commit, harness commit, selection)
panels.description: What exactly ran: the code under test, the harness revision, the workflow and the cluster. Fields stamped by newer ci-observe captures; older captures show 'not collected' for anything they predate.

panels.title: Test ref (requested)
panels.description: osac.ci.test_ref: the osac code under test, as requested (a branch like main, or a PR head SHA in the osac PR flow).

panels.title: Test SHA (resolved)
panels.description: osac.ci.test_sha: the exact source commit the run tested, after resolving the requested ref. 'not collected' on captures that predate this attribute.

panels.title: Harness ref (requested)
panels.description: osac.ci.test_infra_ref: the test-infra harness revision that orchestrated the run, as requested (a branch or SHA).

panels.title: Harness SHA (resolved)
panels.description: osac.ci.test_infra_sha: the exact harness commit after resolving the requested ref. 'not collected' on captures that predate this attribute.

panels.title: Run attempt
panels.description: osac.ci.run_attempt: the workflow run attempt (1 for the first try; the capture ID's a1 suffix says the same).

panels.title: Harness workflow SHA
panels.description: osac.ci.test_infra_workflow_sha: the commit of the workflow definition itself. 'not collected' on captures that predate this attribute.

panels.title: Test filter
panels.description: osac.ci.test_filter: the pytest filter (-k) the workflow requested, if any. 'not collected' on captures that predate this attribute.

panels.title: Test marker
panels.description: osac.ci.test_marker: the pytest marker (-m) the workflow requested, if any. 'not collected' on captures that predate this attribute.

panels.title: OSAC images (specs)
panels.description: osac.ci.osac_images: the image each OSAC deployment was asked to run, one 'deployment=image' entry per line. 'localhost/component-N-pr:NNN' images were built from source in this run. Long values are cut off visually; open the panel's data inspector for the full text.

panels.title: OSAC image IDs (running)
panels.description: osac.ci.osac_image_ids: the resolved image IDs (digests) of the OSAC pods actually running during the capture. 'not collected' on captures that predate this attribute.

panels.title: Image IDs complete
panels.description: osac.ci.osac_image_ids_complete: whether every running OSAC image reported a resolved ID. 'not collected' on captures that predate this attribute.

osac.ci.test_suite: the exact pytest path list the run collected, for example tests/e2e/vmaas/ or 'tests/e2e/vmaas/ tests/e2e/references/' when references ran alongside. It is a path list, not a single suite label. 'unknown' means the workflow wiring did not report the selection; 'not collected' means the capture predates this attribute.
panels.title: Test paths

panels.description: osac.ci.cluster_uid: the identity of the cluster the run tested, so captures can be grouped by environment.
panels.title: Cluster UID

panels.description: osac.ci.workflow: the GitHub Actions workflow name that ran the capture (for example 'E2E BMaaS Full Install').
panels.title: Workflow
Tests and workers
panels.description: The pytest test spans of the capture: every test in start order with its worker, the slowest ones, and the failures.

panels.title: Test timeline
panels.description: Parent test spans ordered by start time, with the xdist worker that ran each test. Captures older than worker attribution show no Worker column or 'not recorded' - that means the worker was not recorded, not worker zero. Tempo returns at most 100 spans per trace, so runs with more tests are truncated here.

defaults.noValue: No parent test spans for this capture. If the Tests card shows a number, this panel is still loading.

targets.query: {resource."osac.ci.capture_id" = "$capture_id" && .pytest.span_type = "test" && name !~ ".*::(setup|call|teardown)" && ( status = ok || status = error || status = unset ) && ( span."osac.ci.xdist_worker" != nil || .pytest.span_type = "test" )}

panels.title: Slowest tests
panels.description: The 20 slowest test spans in the capture, longest first. The span name is the full pytest nodeid; runs with more than 100 tests are truncated by Tempo's spans-per-trace cap.

defaults.noValue: No parent test spans for this capture. If the Tests card shows a number, this panel is still loading.

panels.title: Failed tests, longest first
panels.description: Test spans with status = error, longest first. Empty when the run passed. Note an RPC error can be an expected assertion inside a passing test; GitHub still owns the final job conclusion. An empty table is only evidence of no failures when test spans and the session span exist - see Collection coverage.

defaults.noValue: No parent test spans for this capture. If the Tests card shows a number, this panel is still loading.

panels.title: Fixture work
panels.description: Shared pytest fixtures: how long each fixture's setup took per worker, and how many tests reused it. Fixture time overlaps the runner's wall time - never add it to wall-clock duration.

panels.title: Fixture setup
panels.description: Fixture setup spans ('<fixture> setup', pytest.span_type = fixture) grouped by fixture, with the number of setups and their total time. A Worker column appears once captures carry osac.ci.xdist_worker (Q3); until then grouping is by fixture alone. Fixture setup time overlaps the wall clock of the test that triggered it; do not sum it into run duration. Tempo returns at most 100 spans per trace, so busy runs are truncated.

defaults.noValue: No fixture setup spans in this capture

targets.query: {resource."osac.ci.capture_id" = "$capture_id" && .pytest.span_type = "fixture" && name =~ ".* setup" && ( span."osac.ci.xdist_worker" != nil || .pytest.span_type = "fixture" ) && ( span."pytest.fixture_scope" != nil || .pytest.span_type = "fixture" )}

panels.title: Fixture reuse
panels.description: How many tests reused each shared (session- or module-scoped) fixture. Counts come from pytest.span_type = fixture_use spans, one per test per shared fixture; a Worker column appears once captures carry osac.ci.xdist_worker (Q3). Empty means this capture predates the fixture-reuse instrumentation.

panels.title: Waits
panels.description: What the run waited for and how long each wait took, longest first.

panels.title: Longest waits
panels.description: Every recorded wait span (pytest.span_type = 'wait', or the poll.delay attribute older captures carry), longest first. 'not recorded' in Resource, Attempts or Condition means the wait predates wait-resource identity. Tempo returns at most 100 spans per trace, so long runs are truncated here. This is not runner wall time: waits overlap the tests that waited. Raw pod logs for the run stay queryable in Explore (link under Collection coverage).

defaults.noValue: No wait spans in this capture

targets.query: {resource."osac.ci.capture_id" = "$capture_id" && ( .pytest.span_type = "wait" || span."poll.delay" != nil ) && name =~ ".+" && ( status = ok || status = error || status = unset ) && ( span."poll.attempts" != nil || span."poll.delay" != nil ) && ( span."poll.condition_met" != nil || span."poll.delay" != nil ) && ( span."osac.wait.resource_kind" != nil || span."poll.delay" != nil ) && ( span."osac.wait.resource_id" != nil || span."poll.delay" != nil )}

panels.title: Service requests
panels.description: Service calls observed by Beyla inside the capture: how many, which failed, which were slowest. Service-call errors can be expected inside a passing test; use Failed tests as the run failure indicator.

panels.title: Service-call errors are not test failures
panels.description: Read this row as service evidence, not the test outcome.

options.content: **Service-call errors are not test failures; they can be expected in passing tests.** Use Failed tests and Run result for the test outcome. Everything in this row is service evidence about the OSAC components the run exercised.

panels.title: Calls
panels.description: Named service operations (Beyla): gRPC calls, HTTP routes, Redis and database commands. Excludes pytest spans and wait spans, and Beyla's unnamed internal process spans. Tempo caps search at 30,000 traces and 100 spans per trace, so treat busy captures as a lower bound.

panels.title: Call errors
panels.description: Service calls with an error status. Some errors are expected inside a passing test, so this is service evidence, not the run failure indicator - see the warning above. Use Failed tests for test status.

targets.query: {resource."osac.ci.capture_id" = "$capture_id" && .pytest.span_type = nil && span."poll.delay" = nil && status = error && name =~ ".+"}

panels.title: Calls by service
panels.description: Service calls grouped by service, with the slowest call per service. Empty means no service calls were recorded in this capture. Counts are a lower bound because Tempo caps search at 30,000 traces and 100 spans per trace.

defaults.noValue: No service calls recorded in this capture

panels.title: Slowest service calls
panels.description: Service calls sorted by duration, longest first. Empty means no service calls were recorded in this capture.

defaults.noValue: No service calls recorded in this capture

panels.title: gRPC errors
panels.description: gRPC calls whose response status is not OK (rpc.response.status_code, a string like NOT_FOUND or UNAVAILABLE; Beyla does not set the numeric rpc.grpc.status_code). This is service evidence, not a test outcome; some errors are expected in passing tests. Empty when the capture holds no gRPC calls or none failed.

defaults.noValue: No gRPC errors in this capture

panels.title: Environment
panels.description:
One capture, minute by minute: how many pods existed, what each pod used in CPU and memory, what each node used, and which pods existed when. The collector scrapes the kubelet summary API every 60 seconds, so one point is one minute, and Prometheus keeps 15 days of samples. The time range must cover the capture: a finished capture has no samples in "now", so a range that ends before the capture starts, or begins after it ends, renders empty. Set the range to the capture's start and end, or a little wider.

The **Pods seen** table keeps working after the capture ends because it reads its values with range functions over the dashboard range; a bare instant query of a metric stops returning anything about five minutes after the last sample, which is Prometheus's lookback window, not missing data. The pod series carry no node label, so this page cannot say which node a pod ran on. Node metrics are cluster-wide, one line per node.

panels.title: Pod count
panels.description: Number of distinct pods that reported a CPU sample at each 60-second step. Counted from k8s_pod_cpu_usage, so a pod that exists but reports no CPU sample is not counted. A gap means no samples were collected in that minute, not an empty cluster.

defaults.noValue: No pod samples in this range

panels.title: CPU by pod
panels.description: CPU used by each pod, in cores, one line per pod at each 60-second step. Only the ten pods with the highest mean CPU over the dashboard time range are drawn; the ranking is fixed at the end of the range, so the lines do not swap in and out. A pod that ran for part of the capture has a shorter line.

defaults.noValue: No pod CPU samples in this range

targets.expr: sum by (k8s_pod_name) (k8s_pod_cpu_usage{osac_ci_capture_id="$capture_id"}) and on (k8s_pod_name) topk(10, sum by (k8s_pod_name) (avg_over_time(k8s_pod_cpu_usage{osac_ci_capture_id="$capture_id"}[$__range] @ end())))

panels.title: Memory by pod
panels.description: Memory used by each pod, from the kubelet's working set, one line per pod at each 60-second step. Only the ten pods with the highest mean working set over the dashboard time range are drawn. Working set counts the pages the pod is actually using, so it is the number to compare against a memory limit; the container usage metric also counts reclaimable cache.

defaults.noValue: No pod memory samples in this range

targets.expr: sum by (k8s_pod_name) (k8s_pod_memory_working_set_bytes{osac_ci_capture_id="$capture_id"}) and on (k8s_pod_name) topk(10, sum by (k8s_pod_name) (avg_over_time(k8s_pod_memory_working_set_bytes{osac_ci_capture_id="$capture_id"}[$__range] @ end())))

panels.title: Node CPU
panels.description: CPU used by each node of the cluster, in cores, at each 60-second step. One line per node. This is the whole node, so it is always larger than the sum of the pod lines above: the difference is system work and pods that the collector did not sample.

defaults.noValue: No node CPU samples in this range

panels.title: Node memory
panels.description: Memory used by each node of the cluster, as the kubelet reports it, one line per node at each 60-second step. This is the node total, not the sum of the pod working sets: page cache and system processes are included.

defaults.noValue: No node memory samples in this range

panels.title: Pods seen
panels.description: Every pod that produced any sample during the dashboard time range, with its namespace, its first and last sample time, and its peak CPU and peak memory. This is the answer to 'which pods existed, and when': a pod whose first sample is late was created late, and a pod whose last sample is early was deleted early. The sample times come from the pod working-set metric, which every scraped pod reports. A blank Peak CPU means the pod has no CPU sample: CPU usage is a rate, so a pod scraped only once cannot have one. There is no node column because the pod series carry no node label.
